title: Norfolk Island Amendment (Supreme Court) Bill 2020
portfolio: Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development and Communications

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would make technical changes to the Norfolk Island Act 1979 concerning the Supreme Court of Norfolk Island.
It would clarify that the Supreme Court may sit in a state or territory without an arrangement with that state, as long as no powers or duties are imposed on state officers.
The bill would also confirm that judges of the Supreme Court receive travelling allowances as determined by the Remuneration Tribunal, reflecting existing practice.
changes: The bill would allow the Supreme Court to sit off-island when exercising criminal and civil jurisdictions.
It would permit the Commonwealth to enter into arrangements with state or territory authorities for the effective application of provisions dealing with hearings in a host jurisdiction.
The bill would remove doubt that the Supreme Court may exercise its jurisdiction in a state without an arrangement, where no powers or duties are conferred on a state officer.
It would clarify the basis for determining travelling allowances for Supreme Court judges.
summary.affected: The Supreme Court of Norfolk Island, its judges, and state or territory authorities such as courts and remand centres.

speeches.speaker: Nola Marino
speeches.brief: The speaker moved the second reading of the Norfolk Island Amendment (Supreme Court) Bill 2020, which makes technical amendments to provisions for off-island sittings of the Supreme Court and clarifies travelling allowances for its judges to enhance the effective administration of the Norfolk Island justice system.

speeches.speaker: Jason Clare
speeches.brief: Labor supported the Norfolk Island Amendment (Supreme Court) Bill 2020, which makes technical changes to allow the Supreme Court to sit off-island and clarify travel allowances for judges. Concerns were raised by the Law Council about the removal of Commonwealth payment for witness fees in civil proceedings.

speeches.speaker: Anne Webster
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the Norfolk Island Amendment (Supreme Court) Bill 2020, which makes technical amendments to improve the island's justice system and governance. They highlighted that since 2016, Norfolk Islanders have gained access to federal social security, health benefits, Medicare, and taxation reforms, with 143 JobKeeper and 92 JobSeeker recipients recorded during the pandemic.

speeches.speaker: Warren Snowdon
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the Northern Territory must retain at least two House of Representatives seats, noting its population of 250,000 and 42% Aboriginal residents in remote communities, and criticised the constitutional malapportionment that guarantees Tasmania five seats for 530,000 people. He also supported the Norfolk Island Amendment (Supreme Court) Bill 2020, which allows the Norfolk Island Supreme Court to empanel juries on the mainland and clarifies host jurisdictions and travel allowances for judges.

speeches.speaker: Trevor Evans
speeches.brief: The Norfolk Island Amendment (Supreme Court) Bill 2020 makes technical amendments to the Norfolk Island Act 1979 to allow the Supreme Court to sit in another state or territory, including for jury trials, and clarifies travelling allowances for judges, aiming to enhance the administration of justice on Norfolk Island.
